subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory full reindex gain durable checkpoint/resume state, and should that be always-on internal behavior or a new public `memorySearch.sync` configuration surface?
rationale: The remaining work changes durable memory generation state and may expand public config/status behavior, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive maintainer territory.

options.title: Always-on internal resume
options.body: Implement checkpoint/resume as canonical internal SQLite state with status visibility and no new user config unless a real opt-out is required.

options.title: Configurable resume controls
options.body: Add explicit `memorySearch.sync` controls with docs and upgrade proof, accepting the extra config surface for operator tuning.

options.title: Defer until memory convergence
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause implementation until maintainers settle the long-term default memory backend path.

recommendation.title: Always-on internal resume
recommendation.body: Implement checkpoint/resume as canonical internal SQLite state with status visibility and no new user config unless a real opt-out is required.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sampled history on the memory reindex path and already provided prior issue-review context.
